- When sentiment is positive (≥0.27) and model overestimates, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.70) and model underestimates, increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid missing downside.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), model should not overreact to short-term spikes.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 18 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative spike, model should not lag — forecast should rise faster than historical trend.
- If model consistently overpredicts after sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.80), apply a 1.5x smoothing factor to dampen the forecast peak.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is below model by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, assume mean reversion and adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per day.
